title: Headroom quotas and cold-start risk analysis (April 2025)
summary: Runbook-style analysis of headroom quota settings vs. cold-start risk across three regions. Focused on min/max instance quotas, burst capacity, and the tradeoff between keeping spare warmed nodes vs. cost. Outcome: captured microbenchmarks, per-region recommended headroom, and a small experiment plan for autoscaler TTL tuning.
experiment_objective: Quantify how different reserved headroom quotas (min nodes and soft headroom fraction) affect 95th/99th percentile request latency and cold-start rate during sudden 3x traffic spikes for GPU-backed LLM endpoints.
setup: Summary of setup: We exercised three regional fleets (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) with the same model bundle (gptx-70B-qat). Workload: synthetic spike traces derived from production q1 patterns (20-minute ramps to 3x baseline). Autoscaler under test: new-minmax-autoscaler-v2 with probe interval 30s, scale-up cooldown 90s, scale-down cooldown 300s. Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 latency, cold-start count (node had no warmed KV cache), GPU utilization, queued requests during scale events. Test matrix varied: min nodes {2,4,8}, headroom fraction {0.05,0.15,0.30}, reserve-burst enabled/disabled. Each cell run 6 times to capture variance.

us-west-2,A100-80GB,8,0.15,true,120,260,0.01,72,min 8 with burst gives best UX but higher cost
observations: 1) Cold-starts are strongly correlated with min_nodes and the headroom fraction: increasing min from 2->8 reduced cold start rate in us-west-2 from 18%->1%. 2) Reserve-burst (short-lived warmed burst pool) reduced p99 by ~30% on average when enabled at headroom >= 0.15. 3) Regions with higher image-pull latency (eu-west-1) showed worse cold-start rates even at same min nodes — implies network/registry latency matters. 4) GPU utilization peak drops as headroom increases; cost tradeoff is roughly linear in reserved node-seconds. 5) Scale-up cooldowns of 90s are sometimes too long for step ramps; many queues form within the first 60s — consider faster probe path for bursts.
cost_estimates: Back-of-envelope monthly cost delta vs baseline (min_nodes=2, headroom=0.05): us-west-2 min=8,headroom=0.15,reserve=true => +$14k/mo for that regional pool. eu-west-1 similar sizing => +$16k/mo due to slightly higher pricing. ap-southeast-1 suggested min 4,headroom 0.15 => +$7k/mo. Total incremental cost if applied to all three: ~+$37k/mo. These numbers include GPU instance-hours only and exclude storage/network premiums.
recommendations: Short-term (can ship in 2 sprints): 1) Increase default per-customer regional min nodes for production tiers: set us-west-2=4, eu-west-1=4, ap-southeast-1=3 for now. 2) Enable reserve-burst in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with headroom_fraction=0.15. 3) Add a fast-probe pathway for burst detection (sampled requests with 5s probe interval) to avoid scale-up cooldown limitations. Medium-term: 4) Move registry images to dedicated regional mirrors to cut cold-start image pull by ~40%. 5) Improve local KV cache checkpointing to reduce re-warm time. Long-term: 6) Autoscaler feature: predictive pre-warm based on short-term forecast (ML driven) and customer SLA tag.
